recA5BnM5umys9yRk.Body: Kyle and Serena Denton are community herbalists creating wild-crafted and organic plant medicines out of Milwaukee since 2015. I have used their teas and tinctures on an almost daily basis for years now. Kyle is a great friend of InnerVerse and has appeared on the channel more times than I can count. These products work—not in the allopathic "pharma-medicine" way, but in a terrain-support, consciousness bolstering plant-teacher sort of way.
recA5BnM5umys9yRk.Name: Tippecanoe Herbs
recA5BnM5umys9yRk.Offer Line: Use coupon code "innerverse" at checkout for a 10% discount!

recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Body: The Sonic Slider is the flagship tool behind Biofield Tuning itself, a weighted tuning fork hand-tuned to 93.96 Hz, the twelfth harmonic of the Schumann Resonance, Earth's own natural electromagnetic pulse. Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.
recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Name: The Sonic Slider

I use LotusWei Elixirs to give me an edge with psychic & energetic sensitivity, discernment, and life force coherence. In other words, LotusWei Elixirs help me be a better podcaster and Biofield Tuner. Benefits accumulate over long term use!

recMVdJjP2VZJyI2m.Body: Clive de Carle has spent decades researching high-quality natural health essentials, from magnesium and fulvic minerals to iodine, selenium, and vegan-sourced vitamin D. His supplements are formulated with a focus on bioavailability, so the body can actually absorb and use what you're taking rather than letting it pass through unused. It's a simple, no-nonsense approach to filling the nutritional gaps most modern diets leave behind.

rec6axdrG9jRjnPnr.Bio: Eileen McKusick is the founder of Biofield Tuning, a sound-healing modality that uses tuning forks to map and clear the human energy field, and bestselling author of Tuning the Human Biofield and Electric Body, Electric Health; she has been a recurring InnerVerse guest.
rec6axdrG9jRjnPnr.Name: Eileen McKusick

rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Bio: Chance Garton is the host and producer of the Innerverse Podcast, where for over a decade he has investigated consciousness, mythology, symbolism, terrain health, and the psychosomatic language of the human body and mind. A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Name: Chance Garton
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Role: Host of the Innerverse Podcast, biofield tuning practitioner & researcher

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Sing the Body Electric and the sonic anatomy", "body": "Eileen McKusick describes the newest branch of her work, Sing the Body Electric, co created with the brothers Korn, Isaac and Torold. Together they mapped what they call the sonic anatomy, twelve core tones plus roughly twenty demitones that resonate in specific parts of the body. The sound ma lands in the spleen, which relates to mother, and paw in the liver, which relates to father. There are also five zones people tone from. At Music and Sky she combined a group biofield tuning with mass toning for the first time, watching hundreds of people bounce and sound at once."}, {"title": "Your body as a pipe organ", "body": "The governing image of the conversation is the body as a pipe organ. Macro and micro traumas collapse, clog and rust the pipes until a person expresses only a few notes of their full range. McKusick argues most people have been silenced, in emotional expression and in speaking up for their needs, and that a funny sounding singing voice simply means a pipe is blocked. In her two day workshops everyone sings happy birthday to themselves at the start and again at the end, and she says the difference after seven hours is phenomenal because people stop judging and start playing."}, {"title": "Making harmony out of dissonance", "body": "Chance Garton titled the episode Concordiam a Dissonantia Per Vocem, meaning creating harmony from dissonance with the voice. His breakthrough was treating dissonance as a portal rather than a fault. Before a late night radio appearance, sick and congested, he held his G note tuning fork, which correlates to the throat, and let his voice find the harmony instead of forcing it, moving up and down the register for twenty minutes until his energy was in full flow. He also had a client tone the sound raw for stuck heart chakra energy, and she could not stop yawning."}, {"title": "Tension as the root of nearly everything", "body": "McKusick offers a claim she invites pushback on, that pretty much everything we suffer from mentally, physically, emotionally and spiritually is tension based. Where you are tense, blood and lymph stop moving, electricity and information stop flowing, oxygen drops and disease finds an environment to grow in. Healing then is not removal but relaxation into acceptance. She tells clients the wound of being an unmothered child will never be filled, and that holding a grievance is resistance to the whole stream of life. Even if someone did not deserve forgiveness, your body deserves release from the tension."}, {"title": "Reading the field and the mirror of injury", "body": "Biofield anatomy works as a map. McKusick found a client's left solar plexus blip at baby age and named it, and the woman remembered her mother's postpartum depression. Another man had cleared everything back to age three but never touched the precognitive self worth layer beneath it. Beliefs formed that early even shape your tone of voice, so people hear it and dismiss you. Garton read his own strained shoulder as unexpressed anger with a friend, McKusick read her sprained ankle as dithering over two decisions, and her sore arm as resentment over an apple pie she wrongly assumed her sons ate."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Eileen McKusick returns for her third InnerVerse conversation fresh from the Music & Sky festival, where she debuted a new body of work: Sonic Anatomy, developed with the Brothers Koren as part of their "Sing The Body Electric" project. The premise is that your body is a pipe organ, trauma, silence, and suppression collapse the pipes, leaving most people expressing only a fraction of their full tonal range. The work is about reopening them.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: Topics: why people who were silenced as children carry that silence as physical tension decades later; the 12 tones of the Sonic Anatomy system and which body zones they correspond to; why laughter at the throat chakra is the same release mechanism as crying; how trapped sound drives inflammation, lymph stagnation, and chronic pain; Eileen's own decades-long terror of singing and how she finally moved through it; the "mind as cattle dog", give it a pattern to look for or it eats the furniture; ancestral rivers and mind viruses as inherited tension loops; why even stubbing your toe means something; and Eileen and Chance's real-time examples of reading physical injury through biofield anatomy.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Getting More Sensitive From the Work", "body": "After years of tuning others, Eileen described a growing sensitivity that shows up as tension collecting in her ears, popping whenever she crosses the edge of someone's field or lands on a stuck spot. She compared it to eating clean for years and then reacting hard to a single unhealthy meal, since a finely tuned system registers a grain of sand that a duller one would miss. She warned against turning that sensitivity into empath victimhood, insisting the goal is staying strong while sensitive rather than feeling weak and overwhelmed, and that responding to accumulated damage in the moment beats letting it silently pile up."}, {"title": "A Chronic Ache That Finally Got Witnessed", "body": "A low back pain Eileen had lived with for months suddenly went acute, so she called her practitioner Lori for an emergency remote tune up. She woke the next morning pain free, and Lori explained the blockage had been an old, nebulous weight sitting two and a half feet off her solar plexus, throwing her whole system out of balance and forcing the low back to compensate. That same night Eileen had a lucid dream of working inside the Great Pyramid's King's and Queen's chambers, which Lori said continued the session after the fact. The episode convinced her that healing never finishes, since there is always more potential to access."}, {"title": "Necessary Suffering and the One Thing You Control", "body": "Eileen distinguished necessary suffering, like grief or a genuinely unlucky injury, from unnecessary suffering born of ignorance and unexamined trauma, borrowing an old distinction between natural and unnatural evil. She used her husband's aggressive Jamaican driving as an example of training herself not to flinch unnecessarily, choosing to trust life's chaos rather than resist it. Her larger claim was that vibration and vibe are the only things anyone actually controls, so managing that inner state, rather than the external world, becomes the real lever for change, since making a decisive choice tends to reorganize circumstances around it before the work even begins."}, {"title": "Finding a Core Wound Named Helplessness", "body": "During a webinar, bassist Victor Wooten played a looping chaos riff and then improvised around it until the dissonance resolved into something musical, which cracked open a wound Eileen had never located in twenty five years of practice. The next day, recovering from a motorcycle crash that broke only her left ankle, she traced the pattern back to childhood dynamics she had long overcompensated for as an adult, becoming the most relentlessly helpful person she knows and surrounding herself with people who could help her in return. The insight became a broader diagnostic tool for finding a core wound in anyone."}, {"title": "What Lives Outside the Bubble", "body": "Eileen mapped the feet and knees as some of the densest, most talkative parts of the biofield, holographic to the whole body and often ignored for years before she started working them. She described energy she sometimes finds just outside a client's six foot bubble, which she reads as ancestral imprint from parents or grandparents rather than a past life, though she stays agnostic about the difference. As an experiment she once built up a ball of released energy across sixty feet of approach and had a first time client step into it, sending her into a spontaneous, tearful, star filled experience Eileen credits to the field's own intelligence."}]
